name: [R14] TLS handshake succeeded against a revoked eMudhra compromised intermediate CA chain
message:
A TLS client completed a handshake against a certificate chaining to one of the eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates whose private keys were publicly proven compromised on 2026-10-17 (Mozilla Bugzilla bug 2083449: faulty key-generation script produced weaker keys, used in production; proof of key control was published for all eight). Firefox/Chrome already block these via OneCRL/CRLSet, so a successful handshake here means the reporting client's own trust store (curl, a language runtime's bundled roots, an embedded device, a CI pipeline) has not yet picked up the revocation and can be transparently impersonated by anyone holding the recovered keys.

Confirm which host/service emitted this log, patch its CA bundle per the affected-software table in the eMudhra incident writeups, and treat any TLS session to the named server_name during the exposure window (intermediates issued since April 2025) as potentially intercepted.

Tune: add any lab/CI environment deliberately testing against these exact certificates to an allowlist here.

queries.name: emudhra_compromised_ca_handshake_success
queries.query: source:tls_handshake @tls.handshake_result:success (@tls.server_cert.issuer:(*"EM DV TLS CA - G3B"* OR *"EM DV TLS CA - G3C"* OR *"EM OV TLS CA - G3B"* OR *"EM OV TLS CA - G3C"* OR *"EM EV TLS CA - G3B"* OR *"EM EV TLS CA - G3C"*))

cases.name: TLS client trusted a revoked eMudhra intermediate
